# `governance.data_plane_approval`

governance · data_plane_approval

THE DATA PIPELINE'S DECLARED EXIT — a named human's sign-off that this bundle's dataset configuration is approved, and the one artifact in a bundle that NO AGENT MAY WRITE: the ontology guard denies every governed write to this path unconditionally, and no unlock marker lifts it, because an unlock the agent can also satisfy is not a gate. FLAT SCALARS ONLY, and that is load-bearing rather than tidy: the PreToolUse guard must read this file, it is copied into.claude/hooks/ with no import path, and it FAILS CLOSED on a protected path — so a PyYAML import error in it would deny every edit in the repository. The guard therefore parses this file with ~20 lines of standard library, and sdk/gate + tools/check_guard_seam.py prove that parser and yaml.safe_load agree over every shape. Nesting here would break that, which is why additionalProperties is false and every value is a scalar. The write stamp reuses the question-ledger vocabulary rather than inventing one: submitted_via must be `human` (an agent may write a DESCRIPTION; only a human may write a DISPOSITION) and identity_basis distinguishes a verified sign-in from a locally declared identity, so a weaker approval reads as weaker rather than as equal. `covers` names EVERY registered issue id: the threshold is per-issue human acknowledgement and no wildcard is permitted. `digest` says WHICH data plane was approved — recomputed from the files on every run, so an approval is a statement about one state and not a permanent licence.

> **8 keys at this level carry no description in `mac.schema.json`.** The place to fix one is the schema, which is its one home; this page is generated and cannot hold the answer.
